column4: S4.4: Unicorn 2.1.4 does not quiet a signaling NaN on `fld qword` or on `fst qword` of an SNaN register; the x87 sets the quiet bit (Win32 runner, the instruction itself: `fstp qword` of 0x7fff:8000000000000800 stores 0x7ff8000000000001, the emulator 0x7ff0000000000001; log/roadmap/S4/4_x80probe.py, port/test/test_audio_mixer.py::test_x87_operations_equal_the_emulator). The port follows the hardware (the same rule as S4.6's U-1451; this row covers the x87 unit's fld64 / fst64). Every arithmetic operation, compare, integer store and load other than these two SNaN moves equals the emulator on 60,000 probe records over eight control words (log/roadmap/S4/4_x80probe.py seeds 1..3: 53 / 58 / 70 records differ, all SNaN moves, on x64, the Win32 instructions and the Win32 software path alike; log/roadmap/S4/4_x80probe_seeds.log) and on the 6,000 of the default test. No S4.4 key's vectors move an SNaN (every key equals the emulator byte for byte), so the gate does not see the difference.
column5: A key whose fixture moves an SNaN double through fld / fst would read RED against the emulator while equal to the live CSV; then judge that vector against the CSV hash.

column4: S4.4: at key start the emulator's x87 reads eight registers tagged valid (Unicorn never ran an `fninit`) and the control word 0x023f the CRT start-up stored (bit 6 is reserved and reads 1 on hardware: 0x027f there); a Windows thread starts with an empty stack. The harness empties the tags (TOP 0) after the key's setup and keeps the word. The emulated original's digests of all 55 keys are identical with and without this (log/roadmap/S4/4_tags_check.tsv, SG_S44_RAW_TAGS=1). The live A/B thread's x87 state at the start of each key was not recorded.
column5: Read the A/B thread's fnstenv at the start of a key in a live session.

column4: S4.4: the unit does not model x87 stack overflow / underflow (the x87 stores the indefinite QNaN with IE masked), results outside the extended exponent range (2^-16382 .. 2^16384), or unmasked exceptions; such an operation stops the call (X87Unmodelled, the detail in `$audio/mixout`). Unicorn models no stack fault either (QEMU overwrites the register). No S4.4 vector reaches one (with the tags normalised, U-1431).
column5: Model the stack-fault indefinite once a caller is shown to overflow (sound.dll keeps at most 7 registers in use on the measured paths: a mixer's 5 plus renderChannelVoice's 2).

column4: S4.4: the six MMX renderers (mixRenderRatedC, Voice_renderStream16b / 8c / 16c / 32 / 8d) read two frame slots no instruction wrote when the count is 1 (lane B's next and fraction: [ebp-0x40] / [ebp-0x38] in mixRenderRatedC, [ebp-0x44] / [ebp-0x3c] in Voice_renderStream16b) and store the resulting second output frame past the count. The port takes them as 0; the oracle zeroes the emulator stack before those keys' original arm (ZERO_STACK). On the live thread they hold whatever its stack held.
column5: None needed for the port's own consistency; a live run would show the thread's leftovers.

column4: S4.4: NaN propagation when both operands are NaNs of one kind with equal significands (the SDM leaves the choice open): measured on the Win32 instructions and in Unicorn, the positive operand wins (-QNaN / +QNaN 0x...c000000000000000 gives +QNaN; probe record 186 of seed 45 found it); the software path does the same since. port/test/test_audio_mixer.py::test_x87_nan_ties_equal_the_emulator covers 64 tie pairs (quiet and signaling, both signs and orders, add / sub / mul / div). Two identical NaNs give the same bits either way.

S4.4: the frame block (kFrameVa 0x6E000000, 64 KB) holds the stack locals the renderers pass to a callee by address (renderChannelSingle's / renderChannelVoice's sample cursor, renderChannelStreamed's six DsBuffer cells); a host-served callee sees an address in it where the original passed a stack address. The fixtures' stubs log these arguments as 0 (their skip lists), so the comparison does not depend on the value. Production (S4.10) must keep the range free or map the block itself (the context maps it on first use).
column5: S4.10's host / sink decision on where the port's frames live.

column4: S4.4: Mixer_ctor 0x2c9f0 calls Sound_setSourceType (rva 0x2ad10, through the thunk 0x18a2), which S4.7 owns and has not registered: every vector makes one FALLBACK call (36 over the three layouts). Its result equals the emulated original on all 12 vectors (GREEN_PENDING); the default replay serves the call from the bundle's transcript.
column5: Re-run `test_audio_mixer oracle --keys Mixer_ctor` after S4.7's merge: 0 fallbacks, GREEN.

column4: S4.4: after the MMX renderers' `emms` every x87 register is empty; the unit does not write the MMX values into the physical registers (the hardware leaves them there with the exponent 0xffff). Nothing compares empty registers' contents (the exit check compares registers in use only), and no sound.dll caller of these renderers exists (they are installed only by an unreferenced constructor).
column5: Model them if a caller that fsaves or fxams an empty register is found.
